name: Rajputana Bio.
why: Record quarterly sales, annual sales, annual profit
Management outlook: As per National Biofuels Policy of 2018, there is an indicative target of blending 5% biodiesel into diesel.
Latest quarter Mar 2026: Good (sales +133% YoY, profit +33% YoY)
Sector cycle: Earnings improving but price not confirming
risks: Margins shrinking (16% to 11%) - record profit may be near peak
Working capital stretching - debtor days 82 to 47, inventory days 132 to 132 (rising): check receivables / stock build-up
FIIs (foreign funds) cut holding by 3.4 pts in a year
Domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers) cut holding by 7.3 pts in a year
Cost quality weak: margin shrinking or operating profit falling (costs 85% to 89% of sales)
Micro cap (Rs 134 Cr): thin trading, higher risk - keep the position small
Weak cash conversion: operating cash flow only -105% of 3-year profit

guidance: As per National Biofuels Policy of 2018, there is an indicative target of blending 5% biodiesel into diesel.
Is there any internal revenue target for the next 3-5 years?
capex: We have successfully enhanced capacity at our Phulera and M eerut units by almost 3-4 times.

From April onwards, from coming April onwards, our bids in the OMC tender would be as per our enhanced capacity and we are aiming to produce 130 to 150 kilolitres per day from the coming financial year.
risks: So, what are the key challenges in this sector and why is it that the biodiesel sector is not growing at that pace even when the government has set a target of 5% lending by 2030?
As soon as you see that there is a mandate of blending biodiesel, I don't think you will see a challenge in the growth of biodiesel industry.
focus: As the biodiesel sector evolves in India, we are proactively adapting to diversifying our feedstock sources for better cost control.
So, we are entering a market segment where we are just a drop in the ocean.
We don't focus on all these things that are happening in the market.
